claim: The Platynereis larval visual connectome consists of 71 neurons and 1106 synapses.
source: The Platynereis larval visual connectome consists of 71 neurons and 1106 synapses, and was reconstructed from a tissue block containing the larval head and trunk.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of neurons and synapses in the reconstructed connectome based on the ssTEM data.

claim: The eyes mediate spatial vision by comparing light intensities at the left and right eyes to mediate tail bending during phototactic turns.
source: Using behavioral experiments combined with eye ablations we demonstrate that the eyes mediate spatial vision, whereby light intensities at the left and right eyes are compared to mediate tail bending during phototactic turns.
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral experiments and eye ablation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Platynereis larvae develop four visual eyes that are precursors of the adult's visual pigment-cup eyes.
source: Platynereis larvae develop four visual eyes, the 'adult eyes' (henceforth 'eyes'), that are the precursors of the adult's visual pigment-cup eyes, and are distinct from the more ventrally located 'eyespots' (Jékely et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work and is consistent with the anatomical descriptions in the manuscript.

claim: The Platynereis eyes consist of only 2–7 photoreceptors, a few shading pigment cells, and a lens.
source: These eyes consist of only 2–7 photoreceptors, a few shading pigment cells, and a lens, representing the simplest visual eyes described to date (Rhode, 1992; Arendt et al., 2002; Randel et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and by the anatomical data in the manuscript.

claim: 1690 thin sections (40–50 nm) were collected from a single Epon-embedded 3-day-old larva for ssTEM imaging.
source: Following high-pressure freezing and cryosubstitution, we collected 1690 thin sections (40–50 nm) from a single Epon-embedded 3-day-old larva, encompassing the entire head and part of the first trunk segment.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methods used for the ssTEM reconstruction.

claim: The sections were imaged at 3.7 nm/pixel resolution in a 140 µm × 140 µm × 80 µm volume.
source: Following contrasting, we imaged the sections at 3.7 nm/pixel resolution, in a 140 µm × 140 µm × 80 µm volume (Figure 1A–C; Video 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the imaging parameters used.

claim: 21 photoreceptor cells, 42 interneurons, and 8 motorneurons were identified forming a 'minimal eye circuit' from sensors to effectors.
source: We identified 21 photoreceptor cells (PRC), 42 interneurons (IN) and 8 motorneurons (MN) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1–4), forming a 'minimal eye circuit' from sensors to effectors.
evidence: This claim is based on the manual tracing and identification of neurons in the ssTEM data.

claim: 1106 chemical synapses were identified between the neurons of the minimal eye circuit and their motor targets.
source: We identified 1106 chemical synapses between these cells and their motor targets.
evidence: This is a direct count of synapses from the ssTEM reconstruction.

claim: The neurons of the eye circuit only contain axo-axonal synapses.
source: The neurons of the eye circuit only contain axo-axonal synapses.
evidence: This is an observation from the ultrastructural analysis of the neurons.

claim: With the exception of the photoreceptors, all neurons lack dendrites.
source: With the exception of the photoreceptors, all neurons lack dendrites.
evidence: This is an observation from the morphological analysis of the neurons.

claim: Axons have a median diameter of 160 nm.
source: Axons have a median diameter of 160 nm (Figure 1—figure supplement 5), allowing reliable tracing of most processes.
evidence: This claim is supported by measurements from the ssTEM data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: 69% of the synapses could be identified in at least two and up to five consecutive sections.
source: 69% of the synapses could be identified in at least two and up to five consecutive sections (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of synapse visibility across sections, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5.

claim: Gap junctions were not identified in the eye circuit.
source: We could not identify gap junctions in the eye circuit.
evidence: This is a negative finding from the ultrastructural analysis.

claim: The photoreceptors of the four eyes project to a primary optic neuropil area at the center of the larval brain.
source: The photoreceptors of the four eyes (3–7 per eye) project to a primary optic neuropil area at the center of the larval brain (Figure 1C,E, Figure 2B), consistent with results obtained by the genetic labeling of the photoreceptors (Backfisch et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by the ssTEM reconstruction and is consistent with previous genetic labeling studies.

claim: All photoreceptors from the same eye project along the same axon bundle, forming four separate eye nerves.
source: All photoreceptors from the same eye project along the same axon bundle, forming four separate eye nerves (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is an observation from the ssTEM reconstruction shown in Figure 2.

claim: The eye nerves from the anterior and posterior eyes from the same side innervate distinct anterior and posterior areas in the primary optic neuropil.
source: The eye nerves from the anterior and posterior eyes from the same side innervate distinct anterior and posterior areas in the primary optic neuropil (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is an observation from the ssTEM reconstruction shown in Figure 1.

claim: Some photoreceptor axons cross the midline and project to the contralateral primary optic neuropil.
source: Some photoreceptor axons cross the midline and project to the contralateral primary optic neuropil.
evidence: This is an observation from the ssTEM reconstruction.

claim: The primary optic neuropil is surrounded by three giant glia cells.
source: The primary optic neuropil is surrounded by three giant glia cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the ssTEM reconstruction.

claim: The main targets of the photoreceptors of the four eyes are four primary interneurons (IN1).
source: The main targets of the photoreceptors of the four eyes are four primary interneurons (IN1), with photoreceptors from one eye forming several (up to 30) synaptic contacts to one primary interneuron with a contralateral cell body (e.g., PRCal to IN1pr; Video 4).
evidence: This is based on the synaptic connectivity analysis from the ssTEM data.

claim: The four eyes and the four primary interneurons show a crosswise arrangement.
source: The four eyes and the four primary interneurons show a crosswise arrangement (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an observation from the ssTEM reconstruction shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Primary interneurons have mutual synaptic contacts.
source: Primary interneurons have mutual synaptic contacts (see below) and also form synapses on two other interneuron types (Figure 2E,H; Video 3; Randel et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the synaptic connectivity analysis from the ssTEM data.

claim: The major targets of trans-optic-neuropil interneurons (INton) are a group of contralateral interneurons called Schnörkel interneurons (INsn).
source: The major targets of these trans-optic-neuropil interneurons (INton) are a group of contralateral interneurons, which we named Schnörkel interneurons (INsn).
evidence: This is based on the synaptic connectivity analysis from the ssTEM data.

claim: The Schnörkel interneurons are presynaptic to a bilateral group of ventral motorneurons (MN).
source: The Schnörkel interneurons are presynaptic to a bilateral group of ventral motorneurons (MN; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on the synaptic connectivity analysis from the ssTEM data.

claim: Two motorneuron types were identified: one sends a contralateral projection to both the ciliary band and the dorsal longitudinal muscle, and the other only projects posteriorly along the circumesophageal nerve after crossing the midline.
source: We identified two distinct motorneuron types. The first type sends a contralateral projection to both the ciliary band and the dorsal longitudinal muscle, and branches to send a descending projection to the trunk (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 1). The second type only projects posteriorly along the circumesophageal nerve after crossing the midline.
evidence: This is based on the morphological and connectivity analysis from the ssTEM data.

claim: Both motorneuron types form neuromuscular and neurociliary synapses.
source: Both motorneuron types form neuromuscular and neurociliary synapses (Figure 1H, Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Video 3, Video 5).
evidence: This is based on the synaptic connectivity analysis from the ssTEM data.

claim: The mean diameter of synaptic vesicles in interneurons was significantly larger than in photoreceptors and motorneurons.
source: The mean diameter of synaptic vesicles in interneurons was significantly larger than in photoreceptors and motorneurons.
evidence: This is based on measurements from high-resolution images of synapses.

claim: Photoreceptor synaptic vesicles were not significantly different from neuromuscular synaptic vesicles in motorneurons.
source: Photoreceptor synaptic vesicles were not significantly different from neuromuscular synaptic vesicles in motorneurons.
evidence: This is based on measurements from high-resolution images of synapses.

claim: Neurociliary synaptic vesicles in motorneurons were significantly smaller than photoreceptor or neuromuscular synaptic vesicles.
source: However, neurociliary synaptic vesicles in motorneurons were significantly smaller than photoreceptor or neuromuscular synaptic vesicles.
evidence: This is based on measurements from high-resolution images of synapses.

claim: Vesicular glutamate transporter (VgluT) colocalized with r-opsin1, indicating that the photoreceptors are glutamatergic.
source: We found that vesicular glutamate transporter (VgluT), a marker of glutamatergic neurons, colocalized with r-opsin1, a marker of eye photoreceptors (Arendt et al., 2002; Randel et al., 2013; Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 3), indicating that the photoreceptors are glutamatergic.
evidence: This is based on whole-mount RNA in situ hybridization and image registration data.

claim: Histidine decarboxylase (hdc) does not localize to the eyes.
source: In contrast, histidine decarboxylase (hdc), an enzyme catalyzing the synthesis of histamine, the transmitter in arthropod rhabdomeric photoreceptors (Stuart, 1999), does not localize to the eyes, as shown by image registration and double RNA in situ hybridization (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on whole-mount RNA in situ hybridization and image registration data.

claim: Expression of several monoaminergic markers (TrpH, TyrH, hdc, dbh) was found in the cell body regions of the interneurons.
source: In the cell body regions of the interneurons we found expression of several monoaminergic markers in single cells or small cell clusters. These include tryptophan hydroxylase (TrpH), tyrosine hydoxylase (TyrH), hdc, dopa-beta-hydoxylase (dbh), markers for serotonergic, dopaminergic, histaminergic, and noradrenergic neurons, respectively (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on whole-mount RNA in situ hybridization data.

claim: Choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) and vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT) are localized in the cell body region of the ventral motorneurons.
source: Choline acetyltransferase (ChAT) and vesicular acetylcholine transporter (VAChT), two markers of cholinergic neurons, are localized in the cell body region of the ventral motorneurons (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on whole-mount RNA in situ hybridization data.

claim: Glutamate decarboxlase (gad) partly colocalizes with the ventral cholinergic domain, in the area of the motorneuron cell bodies.
source: A marker for GABAergic cells, glutamate decarboxlase (gad), partly colocalizes with the ventral cholinergic domain, in the area of the motorneuron cell bodies (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on whole-mount RNA in situ hybridization and image registration data.

claim: The eye circuit is a feed-forward circuit where information flows from the eyes to the muscles and ciliary bands.
source: The eye circuit is a feed-forward circuit where information flows from the eyes to the muscles and ciliary bands.
evidence: This is based on the analysis of the directed graph representation of the connectome.

claim: With three different centrality measures (eigenvector centrality, weighted-degree centrality and authority) the four primary interneurons (IN1) ranked among the top five nodes.
source: With three different centrality measures (eigenvector centrality, weighted-degree centrality and authority) the four primary interneurons (IN1) ranked among the top five nodes (Randel et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on network analysis of the connectome.

claim: A search for highly interconnected nodes or communities subdivided the eye network into four modules.
source: A search for highly interconnected nodes or communities (Blondel et al., 2008) subdivided the eye network into four modules (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on modularity analysis of the connectome using an established algorithm.

claim: The four IN1 cells belong to two different modules in the eye circuit.
source: The four IN1 cells belong to two different modules in the eye circuit (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), which together contain all neurons with projections intrinsic to the primary optic neuropil.
evidence: This is based on modularity analysis of the connectome.

claim: The anatomy of the circuitry in the primary optic neuropil displays point symmetry rather than bilateral symmetry.
source: The anatomy of the circuitry in the primary optic neuropil thus displays point symmetry rather than bilateral symmetry (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an inference based on the modularity analysis and anatomical observations.

claim: All four eyes can provide motor input to both body sides.
source: The connectome reveals that all four eyes can provide motor input to both body sides.
evidence: This is based on the analysis of synaptic pathways in the connectome.

claim: The neuronal pathways from the eyes cross the midline multiple times throughout the circuit.
source: The neuronal pathways from the eyes cross the midline multiple times throughout the circuit.
evidence: This is an observation from the connectome reconstruction.

claim: Most Schnörkel interneurons form several synapses on both ipsilateral and contralateral motorneurons in the secondary optic neuropil.
source: However, most Schnörkel interneurons form several synapses on both ipsilateral and contralateral motorneurons in the secondary optic neuropil, representing a bilateral divergence of the connections.
evidence: This is based on the synaptic connectivity analysis from the ssTEM data.

claim: Motorneuron axons receive cell-body-proximal synapses from the ipsilateral Schnörkel interneurons, cross the midline, and receive cell-body-distal synapses on the other side of the body from the contralateral Schnörkel interneurons.
source: Motorneuron axons receive cell-body-proximal synapses from the ipsilateral Schnörkel interneurons, cross the midline, and receive cell-body-distal synapses on the other side of the body from the contralateral Schnörkel interneurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 6G,H; Video 5).
evidence: This is based on the spatial analysis of synapses in the connectome.

claim: There is a strong correlation (Spearman r = 0.67, p<0.0001) between the left and right connectivity matrices.
source: We found a strong correlation between the left and right connectivity matrices (Spearman r = 0.67, p<0.0001; Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis comparing the connectivity matrices of left and right body sides.

claim: The four IN1 cells always receive photoreceptor input in a cluster at the most distal segment of their axon.
source: The four IN1 cells always receive photoreceptor input in a cluster at the most distal segment of their axon (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on the spatial analysis of synapses in the connectome.

claim: IN1 cells receive axo-axonal synaptic input from the crosswise IN1 cell in a cluster positioned more proximal to the cell body.
source: In contrast, IN1 cells receive axo-axonal synaptic input from the crosswise IN1 cell in a cluster positioned more proximal to the cell body (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on the spatial analysis of synapses in the connectome.

claim: Rhabdom volumes positively correlate with axon length and synapse number in photoreceptors.
source: We noted that in our reconstructed specimen the photoreceptor rhabdoms have different sizes, and that rhabdom volumes positively correlate with axon length and synapse number (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of the ssTEM data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Photoreceptors with short axons connect weakly if at all to the primary interneurons (IN1), while photoreceptors with longer axons form more synapses on IN1 cells.
source: Photoreceptors with short axons connect weakly if at all to the primary interneurons (IN1), while photoreceptors with longer axons form more synapses on IN1 cells.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the connectivity data in relation to photoreceptor morphology.

claim: The photoreceptor connectivity-maturation index correlates with rhabdom volume.
source: We defined a photoreceptor connectivity-maturation index (number of crosswise IN1 connections per all connections) and found that it correlates with rhabdom volume (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of the connectivity data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: 3- and 4-day-old larvae swim using their cilia while rotating around their anterior–posterior axis.
source: 3- and 4-day-old larvae swim using their cilia while rotating around their anterior–posterior axis.
evidence: This is an observation from behavioral experiments.

claim: When exposed to alternating illumination from two opposite sides of an assay cuvette, larvae showed directional swimming (phototaxis).
source: When we used alternating illumination from the two opposite sides of an assay cuvette we observed directional swimming (phototaxis) of the larvae.
evidence: This is an observation from behavioral experiments.

claim: Larvae showed mixed behavior, with some swimming towards and others away from the light source.
source: Larvae showed mixed behavior, with some swimming towards and others away from the light source (Video 6).
evidence: This is an observation from behavioral experiments shown in Video 6.

claim: During reorientations, prominent body bending was observed in 4-day-old larvae and weaker bending in 3-day-old larvae.
source: During reorientations we could observe prominent body bending in 4-day-old larvae and weaker bending in 3-day-old larvae, suggesting that larvae turn by contracting longitudinal muscles while swimming with cilia (Video 7 and data not shown).
evidence: This is an observation from behavioral experiments shown in Video 7.

claim: Treatment with mecamylamine, an acetylcholine receptor antagonist, blocked negative phototaxis.
source: In agreement with the cholinergic identity of the motorneurons, treatment with mecamylamine, an acetylcholine receptor antagonist, blocked negative phototaxis.
evidence: This is based on pharmacological experiments.

claim: Mecamylamine treatment increased swimming speed, probably via influencing cilia.
source: Mecamylamine treatment increased swimming speed, probably via influencing cilia (Jékely et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on pharmacological experiments and is consistent with previous findings.

claim: Phototactic efficiency increased with increasing contrast between the light intensity at each side of the cuvette, but was independent of total light intensity.
source: We found that phototactic efficiency increased with increasing contrast between the light intensity at each side of the cuvette, but was independent of total light intensity (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on behavioral experiments shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ablation of the two eyespots did not abolish phototaxis responses in 3-day-old larvae.
source: Ablation of the two eyespots required for non-visual phototaxis in 1-day-old larvae (Jékely et al., 2008) did not abolish phototaxis responses in 3-day-old larvae.
evidence: This is based on laser ablation and behavioral experiments.

claim: Ablation of all four eyes led to the loss of directional swimming.
source: In contrast, ablation of all four eyes led to the loss of directional swimming (Figure 6F), demonstrating that only the eyes mediate this behavior.
evidence: This is based on laser ablation and behavioral experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Unilateral illumination of the eyes triggered reproducible bending of the body in 3-day-old larvae.
source: Unilateral illumination of the eyes triggered reproducible bending of the body in 3-day-old larvae (Figure 6A; Video 8).
evidence: This is based on selective eye illumination experiments shown in Figure 6A and Video 8.

claim: When varying stimulus-light intensities were used for selective eye illumination, graded bending responses with saturation kinetics were obtained.
source: When we used varying stimulus-light intensities for selective eye illumination we obtained graded bending responses with saturation kinetics (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is based on selective eye illumination experiments shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Unilateral laser ablation of both eyes followed by uniform illumination triggered strong and persistent body bending.
source: Unilateral laser ablation of both eyes (Video 9) followed by uniform illumination also triggered strong and persistent body bending (Figure 6B,E; Video 10).
evidence: This is based on laser ablation and behavioral experiments shown in Figure 6 and Videos 9 and 10.

claim: Larvae with unilateral ablation of both eyes were not phototactic and swam persistently in circles when illuminated.
source: Larvae with unilateral ablation of both eyes were not phototactic and swam persistently in circles when illuminated (Figure 6C,D,F).
evidence: This is based on laser ablation and behavioral experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Larvae with ablation of either the anterior or the posterior eye pair showed phototactic responses similar to non-ablated controls.
source: To test if input to both the anterior and posterior eyes is necessary for directional swimming, we ablated either the anterior or the posterior eye pair. We also performed crosswise eye ablations. All of these ablated larvae showed phototactic responses similar to non-ablated controls (Figure 6F), hence the presence of at least one eye on both body sides is necessary and sufficient for directional turns.
evidence: This is based on laser ablation and behavioral experiments shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Upon selective eye stimulation, calcium signals were observed in both the ventral and dorsal longitudinal muscles on the opposing body side.
source: In agreement with the circuit diagram, upon selective eye stimulation we could observe corresponding calcium signals in both the ventral and dorsal longitudinal muscles on the opposing body side (Videos 11 and 12).
evidence: This is based on calcium-imaging experiments shown in Videos 11 and 12.

claim: The strongest mutual connections in the eye circuit are formed between the crosswise pairs of IN1 cells (up to 18 synapses one way).
source: When we analyzed mutual synaptic connections in the eye circuit we found that by far the strongest mutual connections are formed between the crosswise pairs of IN1 cells (up to 18 synapses one way; Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the synaptic connectivity data shown in Figure 7.

claim: The mutual connections between crosswise IN1 cells are formed at the cell-body proximal segment of the IN1 cells' axons, spatially segregated from the more distal sites of photoreceptor input.
source: These mutual, and thus likely inhibitory, connections are formed at the cell-body proximal segment of the IN1 cells' axons, spatially segregated from the more distal sites of photoreceptor input (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on spatial analysis of synapses in the connectome shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: The sub-networks of the crosswise eyes are more strongly connected than those of the pairwise eyes.
source: Modularity analysis also revealed that the sub-networks of the crosswise eyes are more strongly connected than those of the pairwise eyes (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on modularity analysis of the connectome shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Larvae with pairwise ablation of the anterior eyes showed significantly reduced bending relative to non-ablated controls with the average maximum tail displacement reduced to approximately half.
source: Larvae with pairwise ablation of the anterior eyes showed significantly reduced bending relative to non-ablated controls with the average maximum tail displacement reduced to approximately half (Figure 7C,D).
evidence: This is based on laser ablation and selective eye illumination experiments shown in Figure 7.

claim: Larvae with crosswise eye ablation showed stronger bending that was not significantly different from non-ablated controls.
source: In contrast, larvae with crosswise eye ablation showed stronger bending that was not significantly different from non-ablated controls.
evidence: This is based on laser ablation and selective eye illumination experiments.

claim: The strong mutual contacts between the crosswise IN1 cells represent a circuit motif that enhances turning responses during phototaxis.
source: We conclude that the strong mutual contacts between the crosswise IN1 cells represent a circuit motif that enhances turning responses during phototaxis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the connectome analysis and behavioral experiments.

claim: Spatial vision relies on at least two eyes, pointing in different directions, and the underlying neural circuit that contrasts simultaneous light inputs at the left and right eyes.
source: We concluded that spatial vision is not due to the presence of more (3–7 in our larva) photoreceptors in the eyes, since all photoreceptors from one eye synapse on the same primary interneuron. Instead, spatial vision relies on at least two eyes, pointing in different directions, and the underlying neural circuit that contrasts simultaneous light inputs at the left and right eyes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the connectome analysis and behavioral experiments.

claim: The contrast enhancement takes place in the primary optic neuropil circuitry.
source: The contrast enhancement takes place in the primary optic neuropil circuitry, and the INton may relay a contrasted, one-sided signal to the secondary optic neuropil.
evidence: This is an inference based on the connectome analysis and behavioral experiments.

claim: The circuit diverges bilaterally at the level of the Schnörkel interneurons (INsn), when these cells synapse to motorneurons of both the left and right body side.
source: In the secondary optic neuropil this one-sided input could lead to the biased activation of the left or right motorneurons. Our circuit reconstructions partly explain the bimodality of the behavior (either positive or negative phototaxis). Such switching behavior requires neuronal connections between the eyes on one body side and the muscles on both body sides. We found that indeed the circuit diverges bilaterally at the level of the Schnörkel interneurons (INsn), when these cells synapse to motorneurons of both the left and right body side.
evidence: This is based on the connectome analysis.

claim: The sensory-motor strategy of visual phototaxis in Platynereis is similar to that found in the lamprey.
source: The sensory-motor strategy of visual phototaxis is similar to that found in the lamprey (Ullén et al., 1997; Figure 8).
evidence: This is a comparison based on the Platynereis data and published data on the lamprey.

claim: Both the Platynereis and the lamprey phototactic circuits are characterized by extensive midline crossing at several levels, bilateral divergence to allow context-dependent sign switching, and bilateral, probably inhibitory, interactions to enhance turning magnitude.
source: Thus both the Platynereis and the lamprey phototactic circuits are characterized by extensive midline crossing at several levels, bilateral divergence to allow context-dependent sign switching, and bilateral, probably inhibitory, interactions to enhance turning magnitude (Figure 8D,E).
evidence: This is a comparison based on the Platynereis data and published data on the lamprey.

claim: At the cellular level, the Platynereis eye circuit shows similarity in its multi-layered arrangement to the visual circuits of insects and vertebrates.
source: At the cellular level, the Platynereis eye circuit also shows similarity in its multi-layered arrangement to the visual circuits of insects and vertebrates (Figure 8A–C; Sanes and Zipursky, 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison based on the Platynereis data and published data on insects and vertebrates.

claim: Simple eyes, similar to the eyes of Platynereis larvae, are widespread in the planktonic larval stages of several bilaterians and may often function in visual phototaxis.
source: Simple eyes, similar to the eyes of Platynereis larvae, are widespread in the planktonic larval stages of several bilaterians and may often function in visual phototaxis (Buchanan, 1986; Blumer, 1994; Lacalli, 2004).
evidence: This is a statement based on citations to previous studies.

claim: More complex image-forming eyes may have repeatedly evolved from phototactic eyes.
source: More complex image-forming eyes may have repeatedly evolved from such phototactic eyes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the findings and evolutionary considerations.

claim: In Platynereis, visual phototaxis was identified as the first function during the development of the eyes.
source: In Platynereis, we identified visual phototaxis as the first function during the development of the eyes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the developmental and behavioral data.

claim: As in development, also during evolution the first images seen by animals may have consisted of a dark field at the bottom and a bright field at the top of the ocean.
source: As in development, also during evolution the first images seen by animals may have consisted of a dark field at the bottom and a bright field at the top of the ocean.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the findings and evolutionary considerations.
